# Comparing the Two Options

**Principal (P) = Rs 1,00,000, Time (t) = 2 years**

## Option A: Simple Interest at 7%

$$SI = \frac{P \times r \times t}{100} = \frac{1,00,000 \times 7 \times 2}{100} = \text{Rs } 14,000$$

## Option B: Compound Interest at 6.8%

$$A = P\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^t = 1,00,000 \times (1.068)^2 = 1,00,000 \times 1.140624 = \text{Rs } 1,14,062.40$$

$$CI = 1,14,062.40 - 1,00,000 = \text{Rs } 14,062.40$$

## Comparison

| Option | Interest |
|--------|----------|
| A (Simple, 7%) | Rs 14,000.00 |
| B (Compound, 6.8%) | Rs 14,062.40 |

**Difference = 14,062.40 − 14,000 = Rs 62.40 ≈ Rs 62**

## Conclusion

**Option B (compound interest at 6.8%) earns more**, even though its rate is lower — the interest-on-interest effect over 2 years beats the higher simple rate.

**Option B gives more interest by approximately Rs 62.**
